text:
alex-support: Customer reports repeated external tool invocations (payment gateway) after our SDK/runtime retry. They got 2-3 charge events for one user action. Attaching request + logs. Priority P1 — billing exposure.

maya-support: Can you paste the exact request they used? Hosted or Dedicated?

alex-support: Hosted. Raw payload they sent:
```json
{
  "model": "gpt-4o-mini-infer",
  "input": "Charge user for order 12345",
  "tool_call": {"name": "charge_card", "args": {"order_id": "12345", "amount": "100"}},
  "retry_policy": {"retries": 2, "backoff": "exponential"}
}
```
They reported first tool call returned 502, our client retried, then the tool succeeded — but the downstream payment processor shows multiple charge events.

ryan-eng: Do our runtime logs show an idempotency key for the tool call? We should be generating or passing one.

alex-support: Their payload didn't include idempotency_key. Our library currently sets idempotency only for non-tool sync ops. Tool invocations rely on the tool endpoint to de-duplicate. Log excerpt: 
```
2026-02-07T21:30:12Z INFO tool-invoke request_id=abc123 status=502
2026-02-07T21:30:12Z DEBUG retry attempt=1
2026-02-07T21:30:13Z INFO tool-invoke request_id=def456 status=200
```
So two separate tool request_ids.

nina-ml: If the args schema were malformed we'd expect 4xx, not 502. Did customer mention arg types?

maya-support: They said amount was string "100" not integer. But they still saw 502 then 200.

ryan-eng: 502 is gateway error from downstream PSP. That triggers our retry path. Without idempotency we can easily double-execute side-effecting tools. We need a repro.

jules-billing: From billing: we can refund duplicates but need a reproducible sequence + list of affected charge_ids. Also want to understand blast radius — could automated retries cause N duplicates if tool endpoint flaps?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary status: healthy, no global rollback.

alex-support: Repro steps I used: 
1) Send tool call without idempotency header.
2) Configure tool endpoint to return 502 on first call, 200 on retry.
3) Call via hosted API with retry_policy {retries:2}.
Observed two charge webhook events.
Example curl I used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \n -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \n -d '{"model":"gpt-4o","tool_call":{"name":"charge_card","args":{"order_id":"12345","amount":"100"}},"retry_policy":{"retries":2}}'
```

nina-ml: Short-term mitigation: log/warn when a tool call has retry>0 and no idempotency key present (:\warning:). Long-term: runtime should auto-attach an x-idempotency-key per tool invocation when caller omits it, and dedupe identical invocations within a small time-window if retries are triggered by network errors.

ryan-eng: +1. I'll spike a change to emit a high-visibility log line and a metric (tool_retry_no_idempotency). Then propose auto-keying as a follow-up RFC.

jules-billing: I'll process customer refunds once we have charge_ids. Please DM me the list. Also we should notify affected customers and offer remediation.

maya-support: I'll DM the customer asking for full webhook receipts and to rotate any API keys. Alex, compile charge_ids and contact info and I'll own the refund comms.

alex-support: Compiling now. Creating internal ticket: TKT-2026-attach-idempotency-on-tool-retries (private). Will DM Jules with charge_ids.

ryan-eng: :thumbsup: thanks. Action items: (1) Support to collect evidence + refunds, (2) Eng to add temporary logging/metric, (3) Eng to propose auto-idempotency RFC.

billing-bot: Noted — billing alert created BIL-7893 for customer 789.

alex-support: Closing loop here once refunds issued and RFC created.
